label: canon4-art-n2
_why: THE ART-ACADEMY STRESS TEST, take 2 (user-directed 2026-09-04): canon4-je (canon-4rung + the ruled research events, F102 — economically the canon) with ONE change, the art academy's ladder on explicit per-rung multipliers — fine art 5 / 10 / 35 / 80 a level (canon 5 / 10 / 20 / 40; e1/e0 ×2 as the other industries, e2/e1 ×3.5, e3/e2 ×2.3), input value ×1 / 1.5 / 3 / 4.5 (£300 / 450 / 900 / 1,350 at base over the rungs' own vanilla mixes), building_cost 400 / 800 / 2,400 / 3,600 points, ai_value the era rule 1000×2^era, target_be 40 / 30 / 17 / 11%. The user's criterion: e3 profitable but not wildly at a 1930s wage with inputs at +75% and output at −75% — computed: +32% at the French/American 1935 wage, +23% British, +10% at the German top; e2 loses 22–39% there; e0 and e1 die at the floor. Every other industry byte-identical to canon4-je; the private-pool cost divisor PINNED at the canon's 0.000125. The user's question: 'It always bugged me that replicated IP-style entertainment works in game roughly the same as all other, labour-intensive industries. I want to see whether making it realistic would break anything (or maybe to the contrary, it will introduce desirable consequences of unpegging other goods' prices from consumption equilibria, with the price shock of fine art becoming dirt cheap).' config/mod_config.canon4-art.json; tech-tree twin = canon4-je's. n=2 (user: "Build and go with n=2 (not 3)"), 1836 → 1936.1.1.

_arms.canon4-art: {kind: config, config: config/mod_config.canon4-art.json} — canon4-je with the art academy on --tiers-for out=1,2,7,16;in=1,1.5,3,4.5;cost=1,2,6,9 (--divisor 0.000125), research_events transplanted from canon4-je

_delta: vs canon4-je (20260903_173810, n=5): the four art-academy tiers only — output 5/10/35/80 (was 5/10/20/40), input value ×1/1.5/3/4.5 (was ×1.5^k), cost 400/800/2,400/3,600 (was 400/800/1,600/3,200), ai_value unchanged. Recipes, costs, ai_value, techs, companies, research events of every other industry identical.

_predictions.P1_price: Fine art hits the engine's 25% floor in every market holding a film (e2) academy within ~10 years of the first one, and stays there: one e2 level makes 35 a week against the canon's 20, and F19 measured a large market's whole leisure budget buying ~96 at base price. Canon4-je's British fine art ran 133–175% of base all century (at the ceiling in most late dumps), so the swing is ceiling → floor, ~7×. British-market fine art ≤ 30% of base by 1905.
_predictions.P2_death: At a 1935 wage rung 0 needs 96–157% of base and rung 1 56–86% — both die at the floor by price alone; rung 2 (BE 22–31%) sits on the floor and empties through the wage/SoL layoff; rung 3 (13–16%) lives there. Prediction: e0 + e1 share of academy workers at 1935 under 30%; the e3 rung the largest by 1935 in at least one seed; the academy sector's total employment BELOW canon4-je's (fewer levels make more art).
_predictions.P3_unpegging: The leisure need's other goods lose budget to dirt-cheap art: availability is value-weighted at BASE price, so 16× the units at the floor still weigh 16× — services, opium, luxury clothes/furniture, porcelain and radios see LOWER pop demand and lower prices in markets with e2+ academies than in canon4-je (British services price at 1935 below canon4-je's median). This is the 'desirable consequence' half; it either shows in the order book or it does not.
_predictions.P4_prestige: Fine-art prestige output scales with the units: countries holding e3 academies gain a prestige lead out of proportion to GDP (prestige_out fine_art in the summaries); the great-power ranking at 1935 differs from canon4-je's in ≥ 2 of 3 seeds.
_predictions.P5_economy: World and shortlist GDP within the canon's spread (0.65–0.96× / 0.81–1.30×) — the academy is 0.3–0.4% of construction; a stall count ≤ 1 of 3 reported as an outcome. If GDP moves by more than the spread, the cause is the leisure-budget shift (P3), not the academy's own value added.
_predictions.P6_break: Nothing breaks structurally: no negative goods (lint passed), no runaway construction of academies (queue_mix: academies < 10% of any major's private queue), no error-log class new to this arm.

_cost: 2 × 1836→1936, ~2.7 h each: ~5.5 h. LAUNCHED 2026-09-04 with the user's explicit go-ahead ("Build and go with n=2").
_caveats: n=2 against a base of n=5: GDP under ~10% and JE counts under ~20% do not resolve; the fine-art price, the academy era mix and the leisure-goods prices are the readings this batch is for — each is a large, structural effect if it exists at all.
The cost divisor is pinned to the canon's 0.000125 and the dearest academy is 3,600 points (below the book's 6,400 top rung), so the academy scores in the private pool like any mid-book rung.

The market-consumption anchor is unused and percussion cap rides bg_military_industry (12,500 workers); the war channel carries the six army technologies (marines excluded) — both post-F102 fixes are in this arm and NOT in canon4-je's runs.
